ABSTRACT

Modern organizations rely heavily on stable IT infrastructure to deliver business services. When infrastructure components fail—such as databases, payment gateways, or authentication providers—unstructured incident handling causes delayed responses, arbitrary prioritization, technician burnout, and SLA violations.

This project presents the design, implementation, and evaluation of the Intelligent IT Service Management & Incident Resolution System (I-ITSM). Built using Java 21, Spring Boot 4.1.2, PostgreSQL 18.7, and React 18 (Vite 6) with Material-UI, I-ITSM manages the complete incident lifecycle from initial submission through automated triage, investigation, resolution, and closure.

The system demonstrates clean Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) principles and GoF design patterns: 1. Strategy Pattern: Interchangeable technician assignment algorithms (Skill-Based matching vs. Least-Loaded workload balancing), dynamically configurable at runtime. 2. Observer Pattern: Decoupled, asynchronous event publishing for in-app notifications, email audit logging, and immutable system audit trails. 3. Finite State Machine (FSM): Strict validation of 8 incident lifecycle states (`NEW` ➔ `CLOSED`) preventing illegal transitions. 4. Deterministic Priority Engine: Rule-based scoring ( ext{Impact} imes ext{Urgency} imes ext{Criticality}) mapping tickets into standardized tiers (P1 to P4). 5. Intelligent Assistance: Five deterministic heuristics including category suggestion, Jaccard duplicate detection, SLA risk prediction, diagnostic root-cause analysis, and AI playbook assistance.

The application has been validated with 27 automated tests (100% pass rate) and is deployed on cloud infrastructure with persistent PostgreSQL storage.

Keywords: Object-Oriented Programming, Strategy Pattern, Observer Pattern, Finite State Machine, Spring Boot, React, PostgreSQL, Incident Management, SLA Monitoring.

CHAPTER 1 — INTRODUCTION

1.1 Background

In modern enterprises, business continuity depends directly on reliable Information Technology (IT) services. When hardware, software, or network services degrade, Incident Management serves as the frontline operational process to restore normal service operations rapidly and minimize business disruptions.

1.2 Problem Statement

Manual or informal incident management (such as spreadsheets, unindexed emails, or chat messages) suffers from major operational drawbacks: 1. Delayed Triage: Incidents sit unassigned without clear ownership. 2. Subjective Prioritization: Urgent issues are misclassified, delaying critical fixes. 3. Imbalanced Workloads: Tickets are routed without considering technician skill or active queue depth. 4. Unmonitored SLAs: Service Level Agreement deadlines are missed without warning. 5. Duplicate Reports: Major outages cause ticket floods from multiple users. 6. Lack of Audit Trails: No verifiable history of state changes, actions, or diagnostic steps.

1.3 Project Objectives

The I-ITSM platform was engineered to solve these problems by: - Enforcing an 8-state Finite State Machine for incident lifecycle governance. - Computing priority deterministically via an objective multi-factor scoring model. - Implementing pluggable Technician Assignment Strategies (Skill-Based and Least-Loaded). - Providing automated SLA Tracking with approaching-deadline warnings and breach escalations. - Decoupling notifications and audit logging using an asynchronous Observer Pattern. - Incorporating intelligent assistance: category suggestions, duplicate detection, and root-cause analysis.

1.4 Project Scope

The system delivers: - Backend: A RESTful API built with Java 21, Spring Boot 4.1.2, Spring Security with stateless JWT, and Spring Data JPA. - Frontend: A responsive Single Page Application built with React 18, Vite 6, Material-UI (MUI), and Recharts. - Database: PostgreSQL 18.7 with 15 normalized relational tables. - Security: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) across Employee, Technician, and Administrator roles. - Testing & Deployment: 27 automated JUnit 5 tests, containerized with Docker, deployed on Render with Neon Cloud PostgreSQL.

2.4 Incident Lifecycle State Machine

NEW ➔ CLASSIFIED ➔ ASSIGNED ➔ ACKNOWLEDGED ➔ IN_PROGRESS ➔ RESOLVED ➔ VERIFIED ➔ CLOSED
                                                                 │
                                                                 └── (Reopened / Dispute) ➔ IN_PROGRESS
  • Invalid state jumps (e.g., `NEW ➔ RESOLVED`) are rejected via `InvalidStateTransitionException`.
  • Reopening is supported from `RESOLVED` back to `IN_PROGRESS` if verification fails.

CHAPTER 4 — SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE AND DESIGN

4.1 Architectural Overview

I-ITSM follows a clean 4-tier enterprise architecture: 1. Presentation Layer (React + MUI): Client SPA communicating via Axios HTTP client with JWT interceptors. 2. Security & Controller Layer (Spring Boot REST): REST endpoints secured by `JwtAuthFilter` validating Bearer tokens. 3. Business Logic Layer (Services & Strategies): Core domain services, lifecycle state machine, priority scoring, and assignment strategies. 4. Data Persistence Layer (JPA + PostgreSQL): 15 JPA repository interfaces managing normalized relational tables.

CHAPTER 5 — OBJECT-ORIENTED ANALYSIS AND DESIGN (OOAD)

5.1 Object-Oriented Principles Applied

- Encapsulation: Domain entities (`Incident`, `Technician`, `SlaPolicy`) maintain private fields accessible only through controlled accessors and domain methods. - Abstraction: The `AssignmentStrategy` interface abstracts away complex dispatch algorithms behind a simple contract: `assignTechnician(Incident incident)`. - Polymorphism: Runtime substitution of `SkillBasedAssignmentStrategy` and `LeastLoadedAssignmentStrategy` through `AssignmentStrategyContext`. - Inheritance: Domain exceptions extend base runtime exceptions; entity models utilize JPA mapped superclass structures.

5.2 Implemented Design Patterns

1. Strategy Pattern (Behavioral)

Technician assignment algorithms are decoupled behind the `AssignmentStrategy` interface: 
public interface AssignmentStrategy {
    Optional<Technician> assignTechnician(Incident incident);
    String getStrategyName();
}
`AssignmentStrategyContext` dynamically resolves the active strategy from system configuration at runtime without code modification.

2. Observer Pattern (Behavioral)

Incident events are published via Spring's `ApplicationEventPublisher`: - `IncidentCreatedEvent`, `IncidentStatusChangedEvent`, `IncidentAssignedEvent`. - Listeners (`AuditEventListener`, `NotificationEventListener`) consume events asynchronously (`@Async`), decoupling transaction processing from alert delivery.

3. State Pattern / Finite State Machine

Incident progression is validated using an explicit state transition mapping in `IncidentService`. Any illegal transition throws `InvalidStateTransitionException`.

4. Repository Pattern (Structural)

15 Spring Data JPA interfaces (`IncidentRepository`, `TechnicianRepository`, etc.) abstract all database operations behind clean object-oriented APIs.

5. Builder Pattern (Creational)

Lombok's `@Builder` annotation is used across entities and DTOs to enforce safe, readable, and immutable object construction.

CHAPTER 7 — DETAILED MODULE IMPLEMENTATION

7.1 Priority Engine

Priority is calculated deterministically using three standard dimensions rated from 1 to 3:
ext{Priority Score} = ext{Impact} imes ext{Urgency} imes ext{Business Criticality}
Score Range Priority Tier SLA Response SLA Resolution
18 – 27 P1 — Critical 5 minutes 30 minutes
12 – 17 P2 — High 15 minutes 2 hours
6 – 11 P3 — Medium 1 hour 8 hours
1 – 5 P4 — Low 4 hours 24 hours
Worked Example: An outage in the corporate Payment Gateway with High Impact (3), High Urgency (3), and High Criticality (2) yields:
ext{Score} = 3 imes 3 imes 2 = 18 \implies \mathbf{P1 ext{ — }Critical}

7.2 Technician Assignment Strategies

1. Skill-Based Assignment (`SkillBasedAssignmentStrategy`): - Extracts keywords from incident category, service, and title. - Computes matching skill score for each technician. - Selects the technician with the highest match score, breaking ties by lowest active workload. 2. Least-Loaded Assignment (`LeastLoadedAssignmentStrategy`): - Queries active unresolved tickets (`ASSIGNED`, `ACKNOWLEDGED`, `IN_PROGRESS`) across all available technicians. - Assigns the ticket to the technician with the smallest queue depth.

7.3 SLA Monitoring & Automated Escalation

- Scheduler: An `@Scheduled(fixedDelay = 60000)` background task runs every 60 seconds. - Warning Threshold: When \le 20\% of the allowed resolution window remains, status changes to `APPROACHING` and a warning notification is sent. - Breach Escalation: When the deadline passes without resolution, status updates to `BREACHED` and `IncidentEscalationService` elevates priority (P4 o P3 o P2 o P1) and reassigns to a higher-tier technician.

7.4 Intelligent Assistance Features

1. Category Suggestions (`CategorySuggestionService`): Lexicon-based keyword scanning suggesting categories from incident titles and descriptions. 2. Duplicate Incident Detection (`DuplicateDetectionService`): Computes tokenized Jaccard similarity across active incidents in the last 48 hours to alert users of existing issues. 3. Predictive SLA Risk Scoring (`SlaPredictionService`): Estimates breach probability (0.0 - 1.0) using elapsed time, priority weight, and stage inertia. 4. Root-Cause Analysis (`RootCauseAnalysisService`): Matches incident logs against diagnostic error taxonomies (Network, Database, Security, Hardware, Software). 5. Gemini AI Playbook & Chatbot (`GeminiResolutionService`, `GeminiChatbotService`): Generates structured troubleshooting steps for technicians and conversational assistance for users, with deterministic fallbacks when offline.

CHAPTER 8 — SECURITY AND EXCEPTION HANDLING

8.1 Security & Authentication

- Password Security: BCrypt hashing (`strength = 10`) for all stored user passwords. - JWT Authorization: Stateless Bearer tokens containing user ID, username, and role, verified on every request by `JwtAuthFilter`. - CORS Defense: Dynamic origin pattern matching supporting secure cross-origin communication between the Vite frontend and Spring backend.

8.2 Exception Handling

A centralized `@RestControllerAdvice` (`GlobalExceptionHandler`) intercepts domain exceptions and returns structured, user-friendly JSON error payloads:
Exception Class HTTP Status Trigger Condition
`InvalidStateTransitionException` 400 Bad Request Attempting an illegal FSM transition.
`ResourceNotFoundException` 404 Not Found Incident, user, or category ID does not exist.
`DuplicateIncidentException` 409 Conflict Suspected duplicate incident detected upon creation.
`UnauthorizedException` 403 Forbidden User attempts action outside their assigned role.
`MissingSlaConfigurationException` 422 Unprocessable No SLA policy exists matching priority level.

10.2 Three End-to-End Demonstration Workflows

The application supports three complete demonstration workflows: 1. Workflow 1: Standard Employee Incident Creation & Self-Service Tracking: Employee logs in, reports an incident, observes automatic priority and SLA assignment, adds comments, and monitors progress. 2. Workflow 2: Technician Workload Queue, Investigation, & Resolution: Technician logs in, accepts assigned incident (`ACKNOWLEDGED`), starts troubleshooting (`IN_PROGRESS`), inspects RCA/AI playbook, logs investigation notes, and submits resolution details (`RESOLVED`). 3. Workflow 3: Administrative Strategy Switching, SLA Breach Escalation & Closure: Administrator switches assignment strategy from Skill-Based to Least-Loaded, views SLA breach warnings, triggers escalation, reviews audit trail, and marks the incident as `CLOSED`.

CHAPTER 11 — CHALLENGES, LIMITATIONS AND FUTURE SCOPE

11.1 Challenges Encountered

- Asynchronous Event Timing: Ensuring event listeners do not fail if the parent database transaction rolls back (solved using proper transaction boundary design). - CORS in Multi-Cloud Hosting: Managing cross-origin cookie and credential headers across separate frontend and backend domains on Render (solved via `setAllowedOriginPatterns`).

11.2 Limitations & Future Enhancements

- Email Delivery: Currently records simulated outbound emails in `email_logs`; future scope includes live SMTP/SendGrid integration. - Machine Learning Integration: Priority and suggestions currently use deterministic rule engines; future work can train ML models on historical resolution datasets.

---

CHAPTER 12 — CONCLUSION

The Intelligent IT Service Management & Incident Resolution System (I-ITSM) successfully demonstrates the practical application of Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) and modern enterprise architecture to solve real-world IT service management challenges.

Through its modular design, the system showcases: - Clean OO Architecture: Effective use of Encapsulation, Abstraction, Polymorphism, and Inheritance. - GoF Design Patterns: Practical implementation of the Strategy, Observer, State (FSM), Repository, and Builder patterns. - Enterprise Features: Strict lifecycle validation, deterministic priority scoring, multi-strategy technician routing, proactive SLA tracking, and intelligent diagnostic heuristics. - Production Readiness: 27 automated tests passing, containerized Docker deployment, and live cloud hosting with persistent PostgreSQL storage.
